items.followUp: Explain the divide and conquer approach and give one example of how it can simplify a problem.

rubric.why: Shows that the problem is divided into smaller parts.
rubric.description: Explains that a large problem is broken into smaller subproblems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a problem is divided or broken into smaller parts.

rubric.why: Includes solving the parts and bringing their solutions together.
rubric.description: States that the smaller parts are solved and their solutions combined.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the subproblems are solved and their results combined.

modelAnswer: Divide and conquer is a problem-solving technique in which a large problem is divided into smaller subproblems.
The subproblems are solved separately, and their solutions are combined to solve the original problem.

modelAnswer: The two types of HTML tags are paired (container) tags and unpaired (empty) tags.

items.followUp: What result does the logical OR operator give when both conditions are false?

rubric.why: Identifies OR as a logical operator.
rubric.description: Defines OR as a logical operator.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a logical operator.

rubric.description: Explains that OR is true when at least one condition is true.

items.followUp: Name the two types of computer memory and give one example of each.

rubric.why: Defines the function of computer memory.
rubric.description: Defines memory as storage for data and/or instructions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that memory stores data or instructions.

rubric.why: Checks that both main types of memory are named.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both types, allowing main for primary or auxiliary for secondary.

modelAnswer: Computer memory is the storage space in a computer used to store data and instructions.
Its two types are primary (main) memory and secondary (auxiliary) memory.
